Problem Statement
Problem: Algorithms - 17
Let G be a directed graph. Define the transitive closure GT as the directed graph sharing
the same vertex set as G, where an edge u →v exists in GT if and only if there is a
directed path from u to v in G. Furthermore, define a transitive reduction of G to be a
graph with the minimum number of edges such that its transitive closure is identical to
GT. Given that a graph may generally admit multiple transitive reductions, prove that
G possesses a unique transitive reduction if and only if G is acyclic.

0008 | Solution.
0009 | We work with finite directed graphs (digraphs), with no parallel edges; a directed path
0010 | is a sequence of vertices of positive length with all edges oriented consistently along the
0011 | sequence.
0012 | For a digraph G = (V, E), its transitive closure GT is the digraph on V with edge set
0013 | ET = {(u, v) ∈V × V : there is a directed path u ⇝v in G}.
0014 | A transitive reduction of G is a digraph H = (V, F) with the minimum possible number of
0015 | edges such that HT = GT.
0016 | We begin with the classical part of the statement, valid for acyclic graphs.
0017 | Theorem 1 (DAG case). If G is acyclic, then G has a unique transitive reduction.
